name: Medial parapatellar approach for tibial nailing
corridor: Longitudinal cut over the patellar tendon and patella, interval medial to the tendon, optionally through medial parapatellar retinaculum, to a start in the medial aspect of the lateral tibial spine 3 mm medial to the crest

positioning.text: Position so true AP and lateral images of the knee and proximal tibia can confirm the start.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the tibial crest, patellar tendon, and plateau. A guide wire laid along the crest and extended over the knee meets the plateau at the start, typically 3 mm medial to the crest in line with the canal, in the medial aspect of the lateral tibial spine, just distal to the plateau–metaphyseal angle at the anterior joint-line edge.

incision.text: Make a longitudinal cut over the patellar tendon and patella.

superficial_interval.text: Go medial to the patellar tendon. If the patella is stiff, extend through the medial parapatellar retinaculum proximally. Studies have found no difference in knee pain between through-tendon and beside-tendon incisions.

deep_interval.text: Place the opening device in line with the canal. A start that is too medial tends to produce valgus in proximal-shaft fractures.

layers.text: Skin, medial paratendinous interval and optional medial retinaculum, then the extra-articular anterior start.

structures_at_risk.text: A medialized start malaligns proximal-shaft fractures into valgus. The patellar tendon is spared compared with a transtendinous split but can still be injured by a poorly placed cut.

danger_zones.text: An entry medial to the canal axis is the valgus danger zone for proximal tibial-shaft fractures.

retraction_hazards.text: Do not let tendon retraction pull the opening device medial to the crest line.

exposure.text: Gives a flexed-knee nail start medial to the tendon, with optional proximal retinacular extension for a stiff patella.

limitations.text: Knee flexion can still make proximal-shaft alignment harder than a semi-extended method.

indications.text: Used for infrapatellar nailing when the surgeon prefers a medial paratendinous rather than transtendinous window.

closure.text: Repair retinaculum if it was opened and close skin.

complications.text: Complications include valgus malalignment from a too-medial start in proximal-shaft fractures.

procedure_applications.condition: A tibial shaft is nailed through a medial paratendinous window rather than a tendon split

questions.answer: In the medial aspect of the lateral tibial spine, typically 3 mm medial to the crest in line with the canal.
